subject: Eval runbook & staging A/B criteria proposal
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Stone <emma.stone@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Eval runbook & staging A/B criteria proposal

Team — looping you all in. I put together an initial A/B plan and a suggested acceptance matrix for the upcoming Acme staging run (see attached proposed_ab_matrix.xlsx and the draft runbook in the Google Doc link). High-level asks:

- We need a clear pass/fail decision that Product can rely on before we flip traffic for Acme.
- Define the primary metric(s) and thresholds (quality reg thresholds, latency guardrails, token-cost delta).
- Outline required monitoring/alerts during the canary and full rollout.

Context: Acme wants a two-week A/B in staging, then a progressive rollout to 10%/50%/100% production over two weeks if acceptance criteria are met. Their success criteria are primarily qualitative (NPS from internal raters) but they also expect no >2% regression on CTR-like signals and 95th-pct latency < 450ms.

Please reply with concrete thresholds, sampling sizes, and a short owner for each item. If we can lock this by Friday EOD PDT I can schedule the kickoff with Acme for next Monday.

Attachments: proposed_ab_matrix.xlsx
Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-redwood-eval-runbook

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Stone <emma.stone@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval runbook & staging A/B criteria proposal

Thanks Sean — good draft. A few immediate reactions and tweaks from Product:

1) Primary metric: end-to-end human-preferred rate (HPR) on a stratified prompt sample. Accept if HPR delta >= +3% in favor of the variant, or regression <= 1% vs baseline.

2) Secondary metrics: 95th-pct latency < 450ms (as you noted), token-cost delta <= +6% (we need to cap spend). If token-cost delta >10% flag for commercial review.

3) Statistical plan: use two-sided bootstrap for HPR with 95% CI; minimum effective sample per cohort = 1,200 rated exchanges. If we can't reach that in 2 weeks, extend the staging window rather than moving forward.

4) Phasing: staging A/B (2 weeks) -> internal raters only; pilot prod (10% for 3 days) -> broader telemetry + automated checks; ramp to 50% only if automated checks pass for 48 hours.

5) Owners:
   - HPR tooling & rating rubric: Laura (owner)
   - Data & statistical analysis: Marissa (owner)
   - Infra/autoscale & KV warmup plan: Vivek (owner)
   - Customer comms & sign-off: Sean (owner)

I've attached a sample prompt set with the stratification buckets (sample_promptset_v2.txt). Please confirm the telemetry events we need to record (impression_id, prompt_bucket, latency_ms, tokens_in/out, model_variant, rater_id).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Stone <emma.stone@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-06-08T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval runbook & staging A/B criteria proposal

Marissa — +1 on the HPR approach. A few technical clarifications from Applied ML:

- Sampling: ensure stratified sampling by prompt length and intent bucket; include at least 15% long-form (>800 tokens) prompts in the rated sample to catch latency tail effects.

- Statistical testing: bootstrap is fine. Recommend pre-registering the exact estimator in the runbook (median of paired differences for repeated prompts, otherwise mean difference). Also include a pre-specified plan for handling ties and 'no-op' outputs.

- Regression detection: add an automatic early-alert if we see consecutive windows (10-min) with HPR drop > 1.5% and p-value < 0.05. That should pause the rollout automatically (hook to runbook automation).

- Model variants: if we fallback to a smaller quantized variant during capacity issues, we should track variant_id and tag rated examples accordingly so we can disaggregate by variant.

I'll add concrete SQL snippets and the exact metric definitions to the runbook doc this afternoon. Also: confirm whether Acme needs blinded ratings (recommended) or if they want to see labels. Blinded would prevent anchoring.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Applied ML — Evaluation & Quality, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Stone <emma.stone@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval runbook & staging A/B criteria proposal

Quick infra check-in:

- Capacity: we can provision a dedicated staging pool for the 2-week A/B. Recommend a pool sized for peak concurrency + 20% buffer to avoid autoscale cold starts; I'll attach a short runbook (infra_runbook.pdf) that lists the steps to spin this up and teardown.

- KV cache warmup: add a warmup pass of top-1k active conversations before the pilot prod step; that cuts 95th-pct cold-start tail by ~30% in our tests.

- Canary automation: we can wire an automated pause if the monitoring hook (HPR drop alert + latency violation) triggers. That requires a small runbook change and a short Ops playbook for on-call.

- Cost: estimated incremental GPU-hours for the staging pool ~ 420 GPU-hours over two weeks (rough ballpark). If token-cost delta is >8% we should gate the commercial approval as Marissa recommended.

I'm okay with the proposed phasing. I'll own the infra steps and coordinate a dry-run tomorrow morning.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps: 

DECISIONS
- Primary: HPR with stratified sampling; pass if HPR delta >= +3% or regression <= 1%.
- Secondary guardrails: 95th-pct latency < 450ms; token-cost delta <= +6% (commercial review if >10%).
- Sample size: min 1,200 rated exchanges per cohort; include 15% long-form prompts.
- Phasing: 2-week staging A/B -> 10% pilot prod (3 days) -> 50% only after 48h automated checks.

OWNERS
- HPR & rubric: Laura (due: 2027-06-11)
- Stats & analysis: Marissa (deliverable: analysis query + dashboard by 2027-06-11)
- Infra & warmup: Vivek (dry-run: 2027-06-11 morning)
- Customer comms & sign-off: Sean (kickoff w/Acme: 2027-06-14 if we lock criteria)

ACTION ITEMS
- Laura: add SQL snippets and rating blinding recommendation to the runbook doc.
- Marissa: finalize the acceptance matrix spreadsheet and add the exact telemetry event names.
- Vivek: run the dry-run and confirm provisioning cost estimate.
- Sean: schedule kickoff and get Acme sign-off on blinded ratings.

If no objections, I'll mark the runbook as "ready-for-kickoff" in the Google Doc and send calendar invites to Acme and the internal strike team. Please reply here to sign off.

Attachments referenced: proposed_ab_matrix.xlsx, sample_promptset_v2.txt, infra_runbook.pdf
Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-redwood-eval-runbook

—Sean
